title: STAMPED research-object rubric
description: A manuscript-derived pilot rubric for describing STAMPED fulfillment in a research object. Scores summarize this perspective under declared weights; they are not general research-quality judgments or validated measurements.

dimensions.label: Self-containment
dimensions.description: Everything needed is reachable from the research object.

dimensions.label: Tracking
dimensions.description: Component states and the history of their transformations are recorded.

dimensions.label: Actionability
dimensions.description: Instructions and executable procedures make the object usable.

dimensions.label: Portability
dimensions.description: Explicit specifications avoid dependence on undocumented host state.

dimensions.label: Distributability
dimensions.description: Others can obtain the intended state persistently.

principles.statement: All modules and components essential to replicate computational execution MUST be reachable within a single top-level research object.
License declarations for all components are themselves part of the research object and MUST be retrievable alongside the content they govern.
Persistent content identification MUST be recorded for all components.
All components SHOULD be tracked using the same content-addressed version control system.
Provenance of all modifications MUST be recorded.
Code-driven provenance SHOULD be recorded programmatically.
Provenance records MUST include the versions of all components involved.
Research object MUST contain sufficient instructions to reproduce all computational results.
Procedures SHOULD be expressed as executable specifications.
Components SHOULD be organized in a modular structure.
Components MAY be included directly or linked as subdatasets.
Each module's license SHOULD be declared independently and checked for compatibility at the boundaries where modules are combined.
Components governed by different access requirements SHOULD be isolated in separate modules where practical.
Procedures MUST NOT depend on any undocumented host environment state.
Computational environments MUST be explicitly specified.
Environment definitions MUST be version controlled.
Computational results SHOULD be produced in ephemeral environments.
All referenced modules and components MUST be persistently retrievable by others.
Environment specifications SHOULD support reproducible builds.
Each module SHOULD carry an explicit license with a resolvable identifier.

criteria.title: A discoverable object boundary
criteria.question: Can the starting object lead a recipient to the components within its stated computational scope?
criteria.rationale: Self-containment starts at one root; knowledge obtained independently of that root cannot repair a missing connection.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect the root record, README, manuscript availability statement, manifests and their explicit links. Record the scope and the path followed.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No route from the starting object to its computational components is identified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: The starting object names related resources but does not locate the computational components.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: The root locates components, but at least one essential component or its relationship to the object is left implicit.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The root locates all identified essential components and makes their relationship to the stated computation explicit.

criteria.title: Data and code within the boundary
criteria.question: Are the data and code needed for the scoped computations included or explicitly referenced?
criteria.rationale: A published narrative alone cannot supply absent computational inputs or transformations.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Trace every scoped result to its input data and source code. Direct files and explicit external references are equally acceptable. Retrieval reliability is assessed under D.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Neither required data nor analysis code is included or explicitly referenced.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Data or code is included or referenced, but the other category is missing.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Both data and code are represented, but identified essential items are missing or implicit.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All identified essential data and code are included or explicitly referenced, including any controlled-access inputs.

criteria.title: Environment and configuration within the boundary
criteria.question: Are required environments, tools, parameters and configuration included or explicitly referenced?
criteria.rationale: The object boundary includes computational ingredients beyond data and source files.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect environment definitions, dependency declarations, command parameters and configuration files. This assesses presence or reference, not version precision or host portability.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No environment or configuration dependencies are included or explicitly referenced.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Environment dependencies or computation settings are represented, but the other category is left implicit.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Both environment dependencies and settings are represented, but at least one identified essential item is implicit.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All identified essential environment dependencies and settings are included or explicitly referenced; intentional defaults are identifiable.

criteria.title: Reachable license declarations
criteria.question: Can license declarations for the components be reached through the research object?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript explicitly makes license declarations part of the object boundary.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Follow component-to-license references. A root license is sufficient only where its stated scope covers the relevant components; record missing declarations rather than infer permissions.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No component license declaration is reachable from the object.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A root license is reachable, but its coverage of bundled or linked components is unspecified.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Declarations are reachable and scoped for some components, but at least one component remains uncovered.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Declarations governing all identified components are reachable and attributable to those components.

criteria.title: Exact component identities
criteria.question: Are exact content identities recorded for all components?
criteria.rationale: Content identities distinguish a reproducible state from an ambiguous version name.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect commits, checksums, digests, registered content identifiers and submodule references. Include data, code, environment definitions, configurations and results.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Component states have no recorded persistent identifiers.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Only names, moving branches or version labels identify component states.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Content identities exist for some components, but one or more essential components have only ambiguous identities.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All identified essential components have content identities tied to the assessed state.

criteria.title: Integrated content-addressed tracking
criteria.question: Are component states represented in one compatible content-addressed tracking system?
criteria.rationale: A common tracking view makes the state of the whole object discoverable even when large payloads live elsewhere.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect the root version control record and registered data, environment or module states. Git is not required; compatible extensions or equivalent systems qualify.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No content-addressed tracking is identified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Code is content-addressed, but other present component classes are outside the tracking system.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Multiple component classes are content-addressed, but their states cannot all be resolved from the root tracking record.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The root tracking record resolves the states of every identified component through one compatible content-addressed system.

criteria.title: Attributable modification history
criteria.question: Are component modifications recorded with identity, time and a description of the change?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript distinguishes tracking a snapshot from tracking how that snapshot arose.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect reachable histories and provenance records, including large-data or external-module records. Identity may be a stable pseudonym; real-world identity verification is not required.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No modification history is available for the assessed components.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A history exists but lacks actor, time or change descriptions throughout.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Actor, time and change descriptions are recorded for some component histories, but identified gaps remain.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The reachable histories record actor, time and change descriptions for modifications across all identified component classes.

criteria.title: Programmatic computation provenance
criteria.question: Does execution automatically record the commands, inputs and outputs of computational steps?
criteria.rationale: Executable source files describe intended processing; execution provenance records what was actually invoked.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect captured run records and the mechanism producing them. A script by itself is not an execution record. Do not award extra points because the current reviewer reran a command.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No captured computation provenance is identified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Computation is described retrospectively or manually without automatically captured run records.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Run records are captured automatically, but commands, inputs or outputs are missing for some scoped computational steps.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Programmatically captured records identify commands, inputs and outputs for every scoped computational step.

criteria.title: Versions linked to execution records
criteria.question: Do provenance records identify the versions of all components used for each recorded execution?
criteria.rationale: Current dependency versions do not establish which versions produced an earlier result.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect links from run records to the executed code, input data, configuration and environment states, including independently versioned modules.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Execution records do not identify component versions.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: An execution record names versions for code only, or uses unresolved moving labels.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Exact versions are linked for several component classes but a required class or scoped execution remains unresolved.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Every recorded scoped execution links the exact versions of all components involved, including environment and configuration.

criteria.title: Authenticated provenance records
criteria.question: Are recorded identities protected by verifiable signatures?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript describes cryptographic signatures as an aspirational strengthening of self-reported origin, not a prerequisite for keeping useful history.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect signatures on provenance-bearing commits, tags or equivalent records and the published verification route. This concerns provenance records, whereas D-06 concerns distributed artifacts.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Provenance identities are unsigned or no usable signature verification route is supplied.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Provenance-bearing records have signatures and a supplied route for recipients to verify the claimed signing identity.

criteria.title: Acquisition instructions
criteria.question: Are there sufficient instructions to obtain all components needed for the scoped computation?
criteria.rationale: Locating a component is different from knowing how to acquire and prepare it for use.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Follow the object’s documented retrieval sequence, including subcomponents and controlled-access request procedures. Do not require public access.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No acquisition instructions are supplied.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Instructions obtain the root object but omit acquisition of required external components.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Instructions cover external components but leave at least one required acquisition or preparation step unspecified.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Instructions cover acquisition and preparation of all identified required components, including any access prerequisites.

criteria.title: Setup instructions
criteria.question: Are instructions sufficient to prepare a compatible computational environment?
criteria.rationale: Actionability requires a usable recipe for the environment, not only a list of ingredients.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect installation commands, prerequisites, initialization and configuration instructions. Rate their operational completeness; P covers the completeness of the environment specification itself.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No environment setup procedure is supplied.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Setup names tools or packages but omits installation or initialization steps.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: A setup sequence is supplied but leaves identified essential configuration or initialization decisions to the recipient.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: A recipient can follow the supplied setup sequence without inventing essential installation, configuration or initialization steps.

criteria.title: Result reproduction instructions
criteria.question: Do instructions explain how to reproduce every result within the declared scope?
criteria.rationale: A runnable entry point is not sufficient if the relationship to the scoped results remains unknown.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Map reported outputs to commands, their required order, arguments and output locations. Narrow the assessment scope explicitly rather than silently omitting inconvenient results.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No instructions link computation to scoped results.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Instructions cover at least one result but omit other scoped results or their commands.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: All scoped results have instructions, but ordering, arguments or output destinations remain ambiguous for at least one.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All scoped results map to an unambiguous execution sequence, required arguments and expected output locations.

criteria.title: Executable acquisition and assembly
criteria.question: Can supplied executable procedures retrieve and assemble the research object?
criteria.rationale: The actionability section explicitly extends executable specification to retrieval and module composition.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect commands, manifests or workflows for retrieving components and composing modules. Manual authorization may remain necessary; score the procedure after authorized access.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Acquisition and assembly are described only in prose or are unspecified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Executable commands acquire the root but require manual discovery or assembly of its required components.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Supplied procedures retrieve or assemble some required components, with other known steps remaining manual.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Supplied procedures retrieve and assemble all required components from their declared references after any documented authorization.

criteria.title: Executable result production
criteria.question: Are result-producing procedures expressed as executable specifications?
criteria.rationale: Executable specifications reduce the need to translate narrative methods into operational steps.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect scripts, workflows, notebooks with execution order, command files or equivalent specifications. Tool choice and reviewer execution do not determine the score.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Scoped computations are specified only narratively or are unspecified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Executable fragments exist but do not form a result-producing procedure.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Executable procedures produce some scoped results, while other computational steps require manual translation from prose.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Executable procedures specify all computational steps needed to produce the scoped results.

criteria.title: Executable replay of provenance
criteria.question: Can a recorded computation be re-executed from its captured specification?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript names re-executable provenance as the actionability counterpart of inspectable tracking records.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect replay commands and the run specification they consume, including restoration or selection of recorded component states. Judge the capability, not whether this reviewer executed it.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No recorded computation can be replayed through a supplied procedure.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Records expose commands, but a recipient must manually reconstruct their inputs or execution context.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: A replay mechanism exists for some scoped computations, or requires manual resolution of recorded component states.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: A supplied replay mechanism resolves recorded component states and re-executes every scoped computation represented in the provenance.

criteria.title: Separable component boundaries
criteria.question: Are components organized into identifiable modules with distinct responsibilities?
criteria.rationale: Directly included modules and linked subdatasets are equally valid; M.2 permits alternatives rather than requiring a specific packaging mechanism.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect boundaries between present data, analysis, environments, configuration, licensing and results. A file or directory can be a module when its role is clear.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Components with different responsibilities are interleaved without identifiable boundaries.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Some roles are identifiable, but code, inputs or generated outputs remain intermingled.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Main roles have boundaries, but some present component classes have unclear membership or responsibility.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All present component classes have explicit separable boundaries and roles, whether included directly or referenced.

criteria.title: Independent module replacement
criteria.question: Can a module be changed or replaced without editing unrelated components?
criteria.rationale: Independent modules enable reuse and updates without reconstructing the whole object.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect dependency boundaries, declared interfaces and independently selectable module versions. Do not require a monorepo or separate repositories.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Changing a component requires changes scattered through unrelated components.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Boundaries exist, but module consumers depend on undocumented internal paths or state.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Modules have explicit inputs and outputs, but replacing an identified module still requires unrelated internal edits.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Modules have explicit interfaces and independently selectable states; replacement requires changes only at declared configuration or composition boundaries.

criteria.title: Module-specific license scope
criteria.question: Are license declarations assigned independently to modules?
criteria.rationale: A module’s terms must remain identifiable when it is separated or reused.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect per-module declarations or a central mapping with explicit module scope. Identical licenses across modules are acceptable; separate files are not required.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No module-level license scope can be determined.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A blanket declaration exists but does not state which modules it covers.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Some modules have independently attributable license declarations; others remain ambiguous.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Every module has an independently attributable declaration, including explicit shared-license mappings where appropriate.

criteria.title: License compatibility at composition boundaries
criteria.question: Is license compatibility addressed where modules are combined?
criteria.rationale: Having license files does not establish that the assembled object’s combination is permitted.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect compatibility notes, machine-readable policies or documented handling of incompatible terms at actual composition boundaries. Rate declared handling, not a legal opinion by the reviewer.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No handling of license compatibility at module boundaries is recorded.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Module licenses are listed, but their combination is not addressed.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Compatibility is addressed for some combinations, but at least one identified boundary remains unresolved.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The object records compatibility handling for every module combination, including any restrictions or separation needed to preserve permitted use.

criteria.title: Access conditions separated by module
criteria.question: Are components with differing access requirements isolated so that other modules remain usable?
criteria.rationale: Controlled access is compatible with STAMPED; separating access boundaries avoids unnecessarily restricting the entire object.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Identify access categories and module boundaries. If all components have the same access conditions, use the explicit equivalent-outcome anchor rather than invent an exclusion.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Access conditions cannot be determined, or restricted material inseparably blocks unrelated modules.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Different access conditions are identified, but affected components are not isolated.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Access boundaries isolate some differing conditions, but an identified unrelated module still inherits an avoidable restriction.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Components with differing access conditions are isolated and their interfaces are documented; alternatively, all components have demonstrably the same access conditions and no mixed-access boundary exists.

criteria.title: Composable module specification
criteria.question: Can the object’s module composition be reconstructed from an explicit specification?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript’s modularity spectrum progresses from directories toward independently versioned and recursively installable assemblies.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect module manifests, dependency graphs, subdataset registrations or equivalent declarations. Inclusion by value and inclusion by reference receive equal treatment.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No specification identifies the object’s module composition.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A module list exists but omits dependency relationships needed to assemble the object.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Module relationships are explicit, but at least one required module choice or connection must be inferred.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: A complete composition specification identifies modules and their connections so the same assembly can be reconstructed.

criteria.title: Explicit host prerequisites
criteria.question: Are required host tools, operating-system assumptions and resource constraints documented?
criteria.rationale: Undocumented host state prevents adapting an otherwise self-contained object to another system.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect runtime prerequisites, platform assumptions and resource requirements actually relied on by the procedures. Do not require irrelevant hardware detail.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Host prerequisites are unspecified despite procedures depending on host state.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Some host tools are named, but required platform or resource assumptions remain implicit.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Tools and platform assumptions are documented, but an identified essential host prerequisite remains implicit.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All identified host prerequisites and constraints are explicit, including tools, platform features and resource needs relied on by the procedures.

criteria.title: Isolated host configuration
criteria.question: Can host-specific settings be changed through explicit configuration?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript allows unavoidable host coupling when adapting to a host requires changing configuration rather than analysis logic.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect paths, mount points, platform flags and resource settings. An object with no host-specific settings satisfies the equivalent-outcome anchor if its procedures demonstrate that fact.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Host-specific settings are embedded in procedures without an identifiable adaptation route.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Some host-specific settings are configurable, but others require edits to analysis logic.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Host-specific settings are configurable, but undocumented defaults or scattered configuration points remain.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All host-specific settings are explicit and isolated from analysis logic, or the procedures require no host-specific settings.

criteria.title: Complete environment specification
criteria.question: Does the object specify the dependencies required to instantiate its computational environments?
criteria.rationale: A container label or package list can conceal unspecified system libraries or inherited state.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect environments for analysis and result rendering, including language runtime, libraries and OS-level dependencies as relevant. Exact frozen builds are assessed in D-03.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No computational environment specification is supplied.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Only a runtime or top-level application names the environment; required dependencies remain unspecified.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: An environment specification covers major dependencies but an identified runtime, library or system dependency is omitted.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The specification covers all identified runtime, library and system dependencies required by the scoped computations.

criteria.title: Version-controlled environment definitions
criteria.question: Are the environment definitions themselves version controlled?
criteria.rationale: Versioning an output or container name alone does not preserve the definition used to construct it.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect tracking records for each environment definition used in the object. Environment definitions may be stored in explicitly linked tracked modules.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: At least one required environment definition is absent from the object’s versioned records.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Every required environment definition is included in the object’s versioned records or an explicitly linked versioned module.

criteria.title: Machine-readable environment specification
criteria.question: Can environment specifications be consumed by tooling on a compatible host?
criteria.rationale: The portability summary calls for machine-readable specifications where possible, without selecting a particular environment technology.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect environment manifests, recipes, machine images or equivalent specifications and their documented compatible hosts. Rate specification capability, not the number of hosts tested.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Environment requirements are only prose or are unspecified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Machine-readable definitions cover some dependencies but require additional manual interpretation to construct the environment.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: A machine-readable definition covers the environment, but includes an unresolved host-specific assumption outside documented configuration.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Machine-readable definitions can instantiate the specified environment on documented compatible hosts using only explicit host configuration.

criteria.title: Fresh execution environment
criteria.question: Are computations configured to start from a fresh environment derived from the specification?
criteria.rationale: A previously assembled environment can contain undocumented state even if a specification also exists.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect execution procedures and supplied run records for environment creation or restoration from the tracked specification. Reviewer reruns are useful evidence, not a separate scoring requirement.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Execution relies on a long-lived environment whose accumulated state is unspecified.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A fresh environment is recommended but the supplied execution procedure uses an existing environment by default.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: The supplied procedure explicitly creates or restores a fresh specified environment, but this is a separate manual step.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The execution procedure creates or restores a fresh environment from the specified state for every computational run.

criteria.title: Disposable environment lifecycle
criteria.question: Can the execution environment be discarded without losing required results or provenance?
criteria.rationale: Throwaway environments separate persistent research artifacts from disposable computational state.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect output destinations, provenance persistence and cleanup commands. Do not penalize retained immutable images or explicit caches that cannot silently change the specified state.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Required results or provenance exist only in mutable environment state that must be retained.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Some outputs are persisted outside the environment, but required results or provenance would be lost on disposal.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: All required results and provenance are persisted independently, and environment disposal is an explicit manual step.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All required results and provenance are persisted independently, and the execution procedure disposes of the mutable environment automatically.

criteria.title: Independence from previous runs
criteria.question: Does the execution procedure prevent earlier runs from supplying undeclared state?
criteria.rationale: The ephemerality summary requires reproducibility without knowledge of previous runs.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect workspace initialization, temporary files, caches and input/output declarations. A declared tracked prior result is an input, not an undeclared dependency.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Execution depends on files or mutable state from earlier runs that are not declared inputs.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A manual cleanup is suggested, but the required initial workspace state is unspecified.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: The initial workspace and retained inputs are explicit, but establishing the clean state requires a manual reset.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The procedure establishes a clean workspace and only declared inputs for each run; retained caches cannot substitute untracked computation state.

criteria.title: Retrieval in the intended state
criteria.question: Can recipients obtain every referenced component in its intended version?
criteria.rationale: Distributability asks whether the referenced state can actually be obtained, beyond its presence in a manifest or its recorded identity.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect component locations and access routes for the assessed version. Document observed access failures and distinguish authorization requirements from missing resources.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No usable recipient retrieval route is supplied for the assessed object’s components.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: The root is obtainable, but at least one essential component has no supplied retrieval route.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Routes exist for all essential components, but at least one intended version is unavailable or resolves only to a moving state.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Routes provide the intended version of every essential component, including documented authorized access for controlled resources.

criteria.title: Persistence beyond a single mutable location
criteria.question: Are distributed components protected against changes or disappearance of a hosting location?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript names archives, immutable bundles and mirrors as complementary persistence strategies.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect archival deposits, preservation commitments, content-addressed archives and mirrors. A successful download today alone does not establish persistence.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Components depend on unversioned mutable locations without a persistence mechanism.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Versioned component locations exist, but at least one essential resource relies solely on a mutable service without preservation or immutable bundling.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: All essential components have an immutable bundle, archival location or explicit preservation route, but no independent recovery route is supplied.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: All essential components have preserved intended states and an independent retrieval or recovery route if their primary host fails.

criteria.title: Frozen environment reconstruction
criteria.question: Do environment specifications resolve dependencies to fixed states for reproducible builds?
criteria.rationale: An executable build recipe with moving dependencies can construct a different environment later.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect pinned base images, lockfiles, digests, build inputs and external downloads. A published frozen image without a reproducible build definition does not alone satisfy the highest anchor.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No usable environment build specification is supplied.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: A build specification exists but resolves required dependencies through moving or unpinned references.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Top-level dependencies are pinned, but transitive dependencies, base state or other build inputs remain unresolved.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: The build specification fixes all dependency and build-input states and defines their reconstruction without moving resolution.

criteria.title: Resolvable license identifiers
criteria.question: Does each distributed module identify its governing licenses unambiguously?
criteria.rationale: A resolvable license identifier helps recipients identify redistribution and reuse terms without guessing.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect SPDX identifiers, stable license URLs or equivalent references for module and bundled-asset terms. Evaluate identifier clarity rather than whether the license is permissive.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No distributed module has an explicit resolvable license identifier.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Terms are mentioned but their license identities or resolution locations are ambiguous.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: Some modules have resolvable identifiers, but an identified module or bundled-asset license remains ambiguous.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Every module and its bundled assets have unambiguous resolvable license identifiers or stable references to the governing terms.

criteria.title: Coherent frozen distribution
criteria.question: Does the distributed record fix the component versions intended to be used together?
criteria.rationale: A collection of independently changing resources is not the same as a distribution of the intended joint state.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect releases, archives, manifests or root snapshots fixing module selections. Assess the coherent joint version selection here; assess actual component retrieval separately under D-01.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: No distributed record fixes the object’s component combination.

anchors.label: Limited
anchors.description: Components are distributed independently without a declared joint version selection.

anchors.label: Partial
anchors.description: A release or root snapshot selects component versions, but at least one required selection remains floating or outside it.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: A distributed release, archive or root snapshot fixes all required component versions as one coherent joint selection.

criteria.title: Verifiable distributed-artifact origin
criteria.question: Can recipients verify the claimed origin and build source of distributed executable artifacts?
criteria.rationale: The manuscript identifies signed releases and supply-chain attestations as an aspirational distributability property where consumers need origin and build evidence.
criteria.evidence_guidance: Inspect artifact signatures or attestations linking executable distributions to their source and producer. For source-only objects with no executable distribution, record an applicability objection rather than silently excluding this pilot criterion.

anchors.label: Not demonstrated
anchors.description: Distributed executable artifacts lack a supplied, verifiable link to their claimed producer and build source, or no executable distribution is present.

anchors.label: Fulfilled
anchors.description: Distributed executable artifacts carry verifiable signatures or attestations linking them to the claimed producer and build source.
